dialog.body: City of Newport Utilities, water and sewer billing, this is Tony. How can I help you?

Hi, yeah, Tony. Nicholas Barone here. I'm calling because I got a notice, or my landlord got a notice, and now he's saying I owe the water bill. And I don't think that's right. Or I don't know. That's what I'm trying to find out.
Okay, sure, we can sort that out. What's the address of the place you're renting?
293 Farewell Street, up the North End. Second floor, well, it's the whole house, but I'm the one living in it.
Got it, 293 Farewell. Give me a second to pull it up. [pause] Okay, I've got the account here. The account is in the owner's name, not yours.

See, that's what I figured. He told me last week it's mine to pay. Said it's always the tenant. I said, that's not what my lease says, but honestly I haven't looked at that lease since, um, since I signed it.

So here's how it works on our end. The water and sewer bill goes to the property owner. That's who we bill and who's responsible to the city. What the two of you agree on between you, like whether you reimburse him, that's in your lease or a side arrangement. We just see the owner on the account.
Right, right. So the city isn't saying I owe it. He is.
Correct. We're not billing you. If your lease says the tenant covers water, that's between you and him, but the city's bill is his.

Okay. That's helpful. It's funny, my grandfather used to rent on Bridge Street and he'd always say the landlord came by on the first with his hat in his hand, like the hat was gonna help. Anyway. Sorry. Where was I.
No worries. You were asking whose bill it is, and it's the owner's on our books.
Yeah. And honestly I'm annoyed, because he's got a past-due thing on there and he's treating it like I'm the one who sat on it.
I can see there's a balance showing. I can't go into too much detail on someone else's account, but I can tell you the notice would've been addressed to him.

Yep, that tracks. Okay, another thing. My daughter helps me with the bills. She's good with that stuff, better than me. She wants to be authorized, or whatever you call it, so she can call and ask questions. How's that work?

Since the account isn't in your name, you couldn't authorize her on it. The owner would have to do that. But if you set up your own account for something with us, like a trash or other service, then yes, you'd be able to add her.
Huh. So she'd have to ask him, basically.
The owner, yes. He can call or come in and put her name on as a contact. Or if he's okay with it, he can give her permission to talk to us about it.
Which he'll love. Okay. I'll tell her. She's gonna say I told you so, she already thought the whole setup was weird.
Fair enough. Anything else on the account I can help with?
Yeah, one more. If it ends up I'm the one handing over money for it, I work days, so I can't get to City Hall when it's open. Is there a drop box or something for payments after the office closes?

There is. There's a payment drop box at City Hall that you can use outside office hours. Put a check or money order in with the bill stub, or write the account number on the check. Don't put cash in it.
Okay, a check, account number on it. And is that box out front or around the side? I always get turned around over there.
I'd look near the main entrance. If you can't spot it, someone at the front desk during the day can point you to it. And you can also pay online through the city website, any time of day or night.

Online, okay. I'd probably do that. I'm not a big website guy though. I don't even have, like, the news on my phone. I get everything from the radio in the kitchen. That's it. Weather, everything. That's how I heard about, um, the office being closed on the holiday.
Well, the radio works. Yes, we had a holiday closure last week. We're back to regular hours now.
Right. Sorry, I wander. So just to make sure I've got it. The bill's his. City bills him. My daughter has to get him to add her. And I can use the drop box with a check if I ever pay.
You've got it exactly. And if you do end up paying for him, make sure the account number is on the check so it lands in the right place, since it isn't under your name.
Good point. Should I give you my number in case you need to reach me?
You don't have to, since there's nothing open on your end. But if you'd like it noted, go ahead.
Okay, I've got that written down. Anything else, Nicholas?
No, that's it. Thanks, Tony. You cleared up a lot. I'm still annoyed at the landlord, but that's not on you.
Understood. Take care, and happy new year coming up.
Yeah, you too. Bye.
